balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Airbnb, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Airbnb, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

gbv.title: Gross Booking Value
gbv.content:
Gross Booking Value (GBV) is the total dollar value of all bookings made on Airbnb before host payouts, taxes and refunds -- the marketplace's GMV-equivalent and the base off which Airbnb's take rate is applied.

For Airbnb, Inc.: management's own growth narrative is framed around GBV, not revenue -- Q3 2026 GBV grew +21% YoY, an acceleration cited as evidence of Reserve Now Pay Later and the Experiences/Services expansion adding volume.

What to watch:

  • GBV growth versus revenue growth -- a widening gap signals take-rate change
  • Acceleration or deceleration versus the prior quarter, which management explicitly calls out

nightsBooked.title: Nights & Experiences Booked
nightsBooked.content:
Nights & Experiences Booked is Airbnb's disclosed volume metric: total nights of stays plus Experiences bookings, independent of price. Take rate (Revenue / GBV) is derived here since Airbnb discloses revenue and GBV but not the ratio directly.

For Airbnb, Inc.: management attributes roughly 3 points of Q3 2026 nights-and-seats growth to Reserve Now, Pay Later; GBV growing faster than nights booked (average daily rate rising) versus nights growing faster than GBV (volume-led) tells different growth stories.

What to watch:

  • Nights growth versus GBV growth (price vs. volume mix)
  • Take rate drift -- Experiences/Services carry a different take rate than core Stays

adjustedEbitda.title: Adjusted EBITDA
adjustedEbitda.content:
Adjusted EBITDA is Airbnb's own non-GAAP profitability measure (EBITDA adjusted for stock-based comp and other items) and the metric management guides to directly.

For Airbnb, Inc.: FY2026 guidance is for a margin of approximately 36% (raised from "at least 35.5%"); Q3 2026 alone reached a 52% margin, up from 50% a year earlier, with management flagging Q4 margin modestly below the prior year on marketing-spend timing.

What to watch:

  • Full-year margin trend against the ~36% guide, not a single strong quarter
  • Seasonality -- Q3 (peak summer travel) margin is structurally the highest of the year

regionalRevenue.title: Revenue by region
regionalRevenue.content:
Airbnb discloses revenue across four regions: North America, EMEA, Latin America and APAC.

For Airbnb, Inc.: APAC and Latin America are the smaller, faster-growing regions management points to for international expansion; North America and EMEA remain the bulk of revenue. Some quarters are blank where the company did not break out the regional split in that filing.

What to watch:

  • Whether international regions are growing faster than the North America base, supporting the expansion thesis
  • EMEA seasonality (European summer) relative to North America

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Airbnb, Inc.: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Airbnb, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Airbnb, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Airbnb, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Airbnb, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Airbnb, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Airbnb, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
